findings.title: enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path, so SQL expressions can never be enabled
findings.description: The new helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`. When the flag is on, `enabled` is false and the function returns false. When the flag is off, `enabled` is true, the `if enabled` branch returns false, and the function still returns false. The final `return false` makes the feature-flag result irrelevant. The `QueryTypeSQL` case in `ReadQuery` then always returns `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`, even with the flag enabled. The intended result is `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, with the negation and the dead branch removed.

findings.title: DB methods are stubs that always return errors, so TablesList and SQLCommand cannot succeed
findings.description: `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all return `errors.New("not implemented")`. `TablesList` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB()` and `RunCommands`, so it always fails. `SQLCommand.Execute` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `QueryFramesInto`, which also always fails. The go-duck dependency was removed in the same change, so SQL expressions have no working backend after this diff. This should be intentional and documented if it is a staged removal.

findings.title: sql_command.go references the sql package without an import in the hunk
findings.description: The hunk changes `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` to `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and removes the go-duck import, but it does not add an import for `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql`. The file may already import that package elsewhere, but the diff alone does not show it. I could not verify this without reading the file.
